# Errors and warnings

Tool failures are returned as MCP tool results with `isError: true` and a single text block of the form `code: message`. Messages are fixed, client-safe text: they never contain internal URLs, hostnames, stack traces, or platform exception detail.

Warnings ride along on successful results in the `warnings` array, each with a `repository`, a `code`, and a message.

## Tool error codes

| Code | Meaning | Client action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid_input` | The arguments failed schema validation (unknown property, out-of-range value, malformed identifier or cursor), or the requested repository is not served by this deployment. | Fix the arguments. |
| `unsupported_parameter` | Declared in the error model but not currently emitted. | Not applicable. |
| `not_found` | No public record matches the identifier. A record that exists but is not public returns exactly the same response, by design. | Treat as absent. Do not retry. |
| `backend_unavailable` | Every requested repository failed, or an unexpected fault occurred. The cause is logged server-side, never returned. | Retry later. When only some repositories fail, the result is partial instead. |
| `deadline_exceeded` | Declared in the error model but not currently emitted. An overrun request deadline is answered at the HTTP layer instead (see below). | Not applicable. |
| `rate_limited` | The task is at its tool-concurrency limit. | Retry shortly. |
| `capability_unavailable` | Declared in the error model but not currently emitted. | Not applicable. |

## Fixed messages

| Code | Message |
| --- | --- |
| `not_found` | No public record matches this identifier. |
| `backend_unavailable` | The repository backend is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly. |
| `backend_unavailable` | The request could not be completed. (unexpected faults) |
| `rate_limited` | The server is at its concurrency limit. Retry shortly. |

## Warning codes

| Code | Meaning | Client action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend_unavailable` | One repository failed; results come from the others (a partial result). | Say the result is partial. Retrying later may fill it in. |
| `validation_attrition` | Some candidates were dropped because the canonical API did not confirm them as public. Counts are lower bounds. | None needed. Do not treat counts as totals. |
| `cursor_reset` | The cursor did not match the current query, or named a repository that is no longer selected, so pagination restarted at the first page. | Continue from the returned results and cursor. |
| `cursor_expanded` | A repository joined the selection after the cursor was issued. It starts from its first page; the others continue from their offsets. | Continue from the returned results and cursor. |
| `deadline_exceeded` | The federation deadline passed while some repositories were still answering. The result holds what had arrived; the slow repository is named. | Say the result is partial. Retrying later may fill it in. |
| `unsupported_filter` | A filter or facet has no mapping for this repository and was not applied. The rest of the request ran. | Interpret results as unfiltered on that concept for that repository. |

## Protocol-level errors

Requests rejected before a tool runs get a JSON-RPC error, not a tool result: an unknown tool or prompt (`MethodNotFound`), an unreadable resource URI or bad prompt argument (`InvalidParams`), a disallowed `Host` or `Origin` (HTTP 403), an oversized body (HTTP 413), a request that overruns the overall deadline (HTTP 504), and `GET` or `DELETE` on `/mcp` (HTTP 405, because the transport is stateless).
